message.content:
The title of “best” jazz vocalist is always a matter of personal taste, but most critics and fans agree that **Ella Fitzgerald** stands out as the definitive icon of jazz singing. Her impeccable diction, extraordinary range, and masterful improvisational phrasing earned her the nickname “Queen of Swing.” She was a pioneer who set the standard for vocal jazz and influenced generations of singers.

Other names that frequently appear on lists of the greatest jazz vocalists include:

| Singer | Why they’re celebrated |
|--------|------------------------|
| **Billie Holiday** | Her emotive phrasing and unique phrasing turned songs into deeply personal stories. |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | Known as “Sassy,” she combined a wide vocal range with a smooth, jazz‑inspired tone. |
| **Nat King Cole** | A smooth baritone who blended jazz with pop sensibilities, creating timeless standards. |
| **Louis Armstrong** | Though primarily a trumpeter, his gravelly voice and charismatic delivery made him a legendary vocalist. |
| **Diana Krall** | A contemporary artist who blends jazz standards with a modern sensibility, known for her sultry voice and piano skills. |

If you’re looking for a definitive “best” pick, Ella Fitzgerald’s legacy as a trailblazer and her influence on the entire genre make her the most frequently cited choice.
